faq: Can you migrate an app that is already in the stores?
Yes. We keep the same bundle ID and package name, so the new version ships as an update to the app people already have. Nothing is published until you approve it.
Will my users lose their data?
No, that is the main thing we protect. We map every stored item first, move it with a tested script and check it on a copy of real data before the update goes out.
Which old frameworks can you move from?
Native Swift and Kotlin, Cordova, Ionic, Xamarin and older React Native releases are common. Tell us what you have and we confirm the route before you order.
What if a native feature has no React Native version?
We either find a maintained library or write a small native module for it. If a feature is too large for your package, we say so in the plan and quote it separately.

desc:
Migrating your app to React Native moves a native, Cordova, Ionic or outdated React Native project onto a current, maintainable codebase. Ecom Swift LLC plans the move, rebuilds or upgrades the app in your repository and keeps your app ID so existing users receive the update.

## What does it mean to migrate an app to React Native?

Migration means moving an app's screens, logic and data to a new technology while keeping it recognizable to its users. It can be a rebuild of a Swift or Kotlin app, a move from Cordova or Ionic, or an upgrade of an old React Native project to a current release.

The goal is not to make the app look different. The goal is to give you one codebase that is easier to maintain, hire for and extend, while customers keep their accounts and data.

## Why do apps outgrow their original framework?

Frameworks age. Cordova and some hybrid tools have lost momentum, so plugins stop receiving updates. Two native apps cost twice as much to change. An old React Native version may fail to build with current tools and block store updates.

Waiting makes the move harder. Libraries disappear, the gap in versions widens and fewer developers know the old code. A planned migration done now is smaller and safer than an emergency rebuild later.

## How migration protects users and data

Users do not care what framework you use. They care that their login still works, their saved items are still there and the app does not lose anything after an update. Every migration decision starts from that point.

We keep the same app ID, so the new version arrives as an update, not as a new listing. Local data and logins are carried across, and larger packages include a backup and restore test. Reviews, downloads and ranking history stay attached to the listing. How smooth the move feels still depends on the original app, so we test before promising anything.

## What a careful migration includes

- A written plan that lists what moves, in what order and why.
- An inventory of screens, libraries, native features and data stores.
- Replacement of outdated or abandoned libraries with maintained ones.
- Local data and login state carried over for current users.
- Server data and authentication kept compatible with the old app.
- The same app ID and signing setup, so store updates reach existing users.
- Working iOS and Android builds after the move.
- Tests of the main user journeys on real devices.
- A note on any native feature that needs a custom bridge.
- A rollout plan for existing users in the larger package.

## What we do

We begin with a short plan. We open the project, list what must move and flag risks, such as a feature that has no direct React Native equivalent. You approve the plan before any code changes.

Basic upgrades an older React Native app to a current version and replaces broken libraries. Standard moves a small app from another framework and carries local data and login across. Premium moves a larger app, includes server data and a backup and restore test, and adds a rollout plan and a period of bug fixes. We work in your repository, so you can follow every commit.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Back up the repository and signing files before work starts.
- List the features that must behave exactly the same.
- Keep the old app available until the new one has been tested.
- Test updating from the old version, not only installing fresh.
- Roll out to a small group of users first when you can.

**Avoid:**
- Changing the design and the technology in the same release.
- Moving the app to a new store listing by accident.
- Skipping the data carry-over test.
- Choosing replacement libraries only by popularity.
- Throwing away the old code before launch.

## Who this service is for

An owner with a Cordova or Ionic app that no longer builds. A business with separate iOS and Android apps that wants to maintain one. A team running an old React Native version that cannot upgrade without help.

## What we need from you

Access to the repository as a collaborator, a short description of the app and its users, and a list of must-keep features. For store updates, add us in a limited developer role if you want us to upload. We never need passwords, and signing keys stay in your accounts.
